method: Previously authorized official API, imagegen skill CLI generate
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production 2D game terrain material atlas for Night Tide rescue tactics.
Create one opaque 1536x1024 atlas: EXACTLY four columns and two rows of equally sized 384x512 rectangular material tiles, edge to edge, with no gutters, labels, framing, characters or objects. Orthographic straight overhead view, zero perspective. Restrained semi-realistic hand-painted materials, consistent soft diffuse overcast light, cool desaturated blue-gray and muted warm-gray palette. Readable tactile surfaces, moderate detail, low visual noise and no bright specular glare; these sit behind small characters and tactical overlays.
Tile order left to right:
Top row: (1) weathered blue-gray steel ferry deck, subtle riveted panel seams and narrow nonslip lines; (2) worn pale warm-gray clinic ceramic floor, slightly greenish fine grout, no blood; (3) rain-darkened charcoal concrete slabs, restrained cracks and tiny mineral flecks; (4) warm desaturated dock timber planks, damp grain, no pier edges.
Bottom row: (5) translucent shallow teal-gray flood water above a subtly visible concrete bed, sparse tiny ripples and no reflections of scenery; (6) very dark cold navy deep flood water, subtle broad ripples and no shore; (7) solid overhead masonry wall top, weathered wide rectangular gray bricks with clear depth through narrow edge shading; (8) scattered low gray broken rubble over concrete, small fragments and no tall obstacle.
Each tile is a material surface filling its ENTIRE cell. Every tile should tile seamlessly within itself, no unique central emblem or border. Strictly top-down flat game textures, not an isometric diorama, no illustrative scenery, no UI grid, no typography. Keep all texture contrast gentle enough to make gameplay targets clearly readable on top. Entire sheet fully opaque.
scope: Eight reusable terrain materials; preserves map cells and rules; inspected atlas before integration. No human acceptance claimed.
